corrosion_narrative: The average mild steel corrosion rate was 0.6119 MPY against the target of within 3.0 MPY, and the average copper corrosion rate was 0.0200 MPY against the target of within 0.5 MPY. Status: Excellent. Corrosion control was Excellent because both metals remained below their target limits during the August reporting period. Mild steel corrosion increased later in the month while copper corrosion decreased, so the mild steel movement should continue to be compared with product residual and ORP trends.
corrosion_chart_comment: Corrosion remained within target, with mild steel increasing later in the month.
scale_narrative: Status: Acceptable. Traced Product averaged 90.26 ppm against the 82.00-88.00 ppm Controller Setpoint control range, with 29.9% of readings within range. Traced Product remained above the configured range at the end of the month, moving from about 89.6 ppm early to 90.9 ppm later. Conductivity was also not maintained and stayed below its configured range, so the Traced Product variation should be tied to conductivity control before assigning another feed-control cause.
scale_chart_comment: Traced Product remained high and was still not consistently maintained at month end.
microbial_narrative: FRC data was not available in the field data for this reporting period and will be checked during the upcoming service visit. ORP did not show a strong spike response pattern during the month, but biocide relay activity was present, supporting an Acceptable microbial control status pending field residual confirmation. Copper corrosion remained within target, indicating no copper corrosion upset was observed during the reporting period.
orp_chart_comment: ORP response was not strong and should be verified with field FRC testing.
water_efficiency_narrative: Water efficiency was Critical. Conductivity averaged 891.67 uS/cm against the 930.00-970.00 uS/cm Controller Setpoint range, with only 13.2% of readings in range. Conductivity stayed below the configured range and moved slightly from about 889.4 uS/cm early to 893.9 uS/cm later in the month. Makeup conductivity was not available, so actual cycles of concentration could not be calculated; dilution, water loss, excess blowdown, or makeup changes should be reviewed.
conductivity_chart_comment: Conductivity remained below the controller setpoint range and needs attention.
product_efficiency_narrative: Product efficiency needs attention because Traced Product averaged 90.26 ppm against the 85.00 ppm setpoint and the 82.00-88.00 ppm control range, with only 29.9% of readings in range. Polymer consumption rate averaged 62.5%, so phosphate, silica, and product residuals should be verified during the next service visit. Because conductivity was also not maintained, product-control review should first be tied to conductivity, blowdown, makeup, dilution, or water-loss behavior before changing feed settings.
proactive_support_narrative: No service notes were recorded for the August reporting period. Recommended follow-up: review conductivity control first by checking makeup conditions, blowdown settings, dilution, and possible water loss; then verify Traced Product response after conductivity control improves. Check FRC and dip-slide CFU during the upcoming service visit to confirm microbial control, capture makeup conductivity so actual cycles of concentration can be verified, and verify phosphate and silica residuals against the polymer consumption trend.
closing_summary: Overall August performance for Flowserve showed Excellent corrosion control and Acceptable microbial control, while water efficiency and Traced Product consistency need follow-up. The primary action is to investigate low conductivity and possible dilution, excess blowdown, makeup change, or water loss, then confirm product residual response after conductivity control is stabilized.
